By Oliver Fairfax~n~~n~It's been over 60 years since the death of President Joe S. Russo. There are few who don't know the haunting image of the President's body floating in the swimming pool of the Lampedusa Hotel in Vice City.~n~~n~Mystery still shrouds the circumstances of the President's death. He was wildly popular in his time, seen as young, charismatic and attractive. But his life was tragically cut short in his swimming shorts that day in November of 1965. The official line is that he was assassinated by a Communist Cuban strike team masquerading as a rumba band. But there are many who cast doubt on this official account. If the Cuban assassins had undertaken the hit to destabilize the US government and escalate the Cold War why didn't the US retaliate? It's not like the US doesn't bomb the shit out of whoever we like.~n~~n~There are many theories, one concerning the Cubans but on the right wing, not the Communist administration. Some have asserted that, yes President Russo was killed by the rumba band, but that they were in fact far-right Cuban dissidents angry with Russo's live-and-let-live attitude to the Communists in Cuba. But this ignores the fact that Russo had many supporters among the Cuban refugees and regularly referred to the Communist Cubans as "Havana Humpdicks".~n~~n~Then there are the theories related to the fact that Russo's autopsy revealed traces of paprika pepper in his stomach. This is a spice popular in Eastern European dishes, leading to theories that Russo was in fact poisoned by a Hungarian secret agent, working for the Russians. But this ignores the fact that paprika is used in many American dishes, like BBQ and Tex Mex cooking.~n~~n~Another theory involves the owner of the Lampedusa Hotel and his famous clientele. Despite being married, Russo had been connected with a famous starlet – Peggy Aydeen – who was also engaged to Herbie Butler, the owner of the Lampedusa. Could Butler have paid the band or poisoned the paprika? Whatever the full story is, it died that day with President Russo on November 21,1965. R.I.P. J.S.R.

By Francis Dallal~n~~n~No one remembers when M7 came to Hamlet. But the sight of tattooed slabs of muscle standing on every street corner, with gold-toothed smiles on their faces and guns in their low-slung pockets, has become the norm. Arturo had a firm handshake and a kind face, but behind his smile I detected anxiety tinged with sadness and a hint of defeat. Sipping a café de olla, Arturo explained how his grocery store survived Hurricane Roxy but might not endure the M7-shaped storm clouds gathering.~n~~n~"Every time they arrest one of these thugs, two take their place. We're terrified. Walking around... it feels like we're in an open prison, and they're the wardens. "You're not safe here, my friend. They're watching now." I look over to see two pumped dudes on the other side of the street. Suddenly there's a bang. A car's backfired. But it's too much for Arturo. He drops a $5 bill on the table and gets up to leave the cafeteria. "I'm sorry. I need to open my bodega. By Quentin Felz~n~~n~There is a mythical city reputed to be in the jungle of the Amazonian Rainforest. It goes by the name of El Dorado – the Golden One. Many have sought it over the centuries, and many have perished in their pursuit, but still it holds a pull on the hearts of men greedy for adventure, greedy for riches, but mainly greedy for knowledge of their own limits.~n~~n~And such a place exists far closer to home, in the wilds of Leonida.~n~~n~It is called the Thrillbilly Mud Club.~n~~n~In America, you will find a special type of person who is on a quest to find the heart of our great country. Not geographically, but spiritually. The Thrillbilly Mud Club is the closest you'll ever get to the essence of these united states. It's where working men and women commune with dirt bikes, off-road vehicles, fireworks, and warm beer. These are the new visionaries and poets of our age – the revving of their engines is the scream of a forgotten generation demanding America's attention. And I couldn't wait to meet them as I drove my RV through the entrance arch proudly draped in flags.~n~~n~What I discovered may surprise you. Yes, there was a high level of avoidable injuries, but there was also a deeper wound that ran through all these dirt-encrusted philosopher-kings – that wound is called 'hope'. Hope for a better tomorrow? Sure. But also a hope for a better present, where a gnarly 360 on a dirt bike, or catching air in a monster truck, is all the American Dream these wasted warriors need.~n~~n~And what of the Queens of the Quagmire? Not a moment passes without a stars and stripes bikini-top being held aloft like a US flag hoisted by our brave soldiers on some far-flung Pacific Island.~n~~n~By four in the morning, I had supped my fill of this swamp-bound bacchanal, but any hope of rest was short-lived as I watched my RV being torched by an enthusiastic crowd – an act I took as one of acceptance. As the dawn light probed over the final flames, I walked to the highway, wiser, and without my pants that had also been taken. In the distance I see those pants being held aloft by a bearded tattooed demi-god. As the crowd cheered so did I, for the Thrillbilly Mud Club had claimed the pants, and my heart with them.

Had she fled? Had one of the banditos ridden off with her? Was she one of the unidentifiable bodies heaped against the wall? Rust was never to know. She was gone. That was all... Then, too, his cheeks had been slapped, but by a fairer hand... And wasn't that just the way of things, he thought. We exchange the promised hands of those we love for our own, calloused dukes, and the tender sting of a lover's embrace for the disintegrating skull of the last death-face desperado as we beat him to death atop the bodies of his comrades... When daybreak arrives in New Austin, it arrives fast. Sunlight broke over the eastern horizon and swept over the desert, painting the yuccas and the scrub brush in light the color of a golden Palomino mare in heat, then hastening westward to fully illuminate the land with the speed and urgency of a golden Palomino stallion in full, ecstatic mount. Rust McCreary stood upon the ridge, surveying the morning, as much a part of this desolate frontier as the tumbleweeds on the main street, or the vultures huddled on the telegraph wires, or the blood drying in the sand, or the elegiac whisper of his own inner monologue.~n~An astute observer — had one existed — might have asked themselves which untamed wilderness the man was really contemplating: the dusty, unending desert without, or the dusty, unending desert within. But then, after all, Rust pondered, weren't they the same thing?~n~"America..." he muttered, to no one, and for no reason at all. Once, a foolish youth had believed that the frontier was the line between civilization and savagery. Now, forty years later, things weren't so simple. Had the arid dustbowl of New Austin finally blown across his heart? Or had the barren emptiness of their souls turned the land to dust? Or — perhaps — had the desert within and the desert without simply met and blurred into one another? And if so, what hope for him? How long could a man remain a man on the border between two such storms? Was his voice merely another lonely sound on the frontier of the American soul, like a coyote in the night? And was that why everyone was always telling him to shut up? The gentle chirping of the cicadas was his only answer. That, and the demented screaming of the man mounting the gallows...

Liberty, Gellhorn, Alderney and Carcer had parachuted down into occupied Europe — either France or an even meeker country — and were immediately captured. They had escaped, killed over 5000 Arschlochkommandos in the process, before getting captured again. This time their prison camp had a fence, which made escape much harder.~n~~n~The Germans had rightfully identified Gellhorn as the main troublemaker, and put him in isolation, hoping to break his spirit. The mad Leonidan, however, soon turned the tables on his captors. Day in and day out, the guards outside his cell were driven mad by the unremitting sound of Gellhorn's frenzied pumping, pausing only now and again for a breathless rendition of "The Star-Spangled Banner". When the last prison camp guard had finally succumbed — shrieking "Nein!" and shooting himself — Liberty had smartly identified his golden opportunity, commandeering their Übermacht motorbike and making an all-American jump straight through the fence. Loading up on guns, ammunition, explosives, cigars and Bratwurst, they were ready for phase three of the plan.~n~~n~Then there had been the hard and bloody tank battle at Panzerschlong. The surprisingly straightforward bombing of the dam at Wimpfken-Shmimpfken. The humbling moment of near defeat before the triumphant comeback at the compound in Klimaxburg.~n~~n~And then, the pièce de résistance: the final stage of their grand plan to win the war. At its heart, it was deceptively simple: the highest-ranking members of Germany's political and military spheres were to be summoned to a remote château in the hills to attend a lavish dinner party hosted in celebration of the Führer himself.
